title: Default privileges: the permission that appears with the next table

videos.script: Lesson 12 left every role with exactly what it needs. That lasts until the next migration. {{migration}} A grant on all tables in a schema sounds like a rule. It is a loop that ran once. The table created tomorrow gets nothing, and the application finds out in production. {{tomorrow}} This lesson fixes that with default privileges. You tell the server, once, what every new table should give, and to whom. {{defaults}} Then you fall into the trap this feature is known for. A default belongs to the role that creates the table, not to the schema. Create the table as somebody else, and nothing is granted. {{trap}} You read the defaults back, including one nobody wrote down: every new function can be called by everybody. Then you remove a role that owns things. The server refuses, and its refusal turns out to be the best inventory you have. {{inventory}} And you meet the predefined roles. One reads everything. One sees every session. One can stop them. Each of them used to be a reason to hand out superuser. {{title}}
